        **Abstract**: The expressive power and computational complexity of deep visual generative models, such
as ﬂow-based and autoregressive (AR) models, have gained considerable interest for their wide-
ranging applications in generative tasks.
However, the theoretical characterization of their
expressiveness through the lens of circuit complexity remains underexplored, particularly for
the state-of-the-art architecture like FlowAR proposed by [Ren et al., 2024], which integrates
ﬂow-based and autoregressive mechanisms. This gap limits our understanding of their inherent
computational limits and practical eﬃciency. In this study, we address this gap by analyzing the
circuit complexity of the FlowAR architecture. We demonstrate that when the largest feature
map produced by the FlowAR model has dimensions n × n × c, the FlowAR model is simulable
by a family of threshold circuits TC0, which have constant depth O(1) and polynomial width
poly(n). This is the ﬁrst study to rigorously highlight the limitations in the expressive power
of FlowAR models. Furthermore, we identify the conditions under which the FlowAR model
computations can achieve almost quadratic time. To validate our theoretical ﬁndings, we present
eﬃcient model variant constructions based on low-rank approximations that align with the
derived criteria. Our work provides a foundation for future comparisons with other generative
paradigms and guides the development of more eﬃcient and expressive implementations.

**Structured Highlights for the Research Paper:**

**Title:** On Computational Limits of FlowAR Models: Expressivity and Efficiency

---

**1. Core Innovation:**  
The paper introduces a rigorous analysis of the circuit complexity of the FlowAR model, integrating flow-based and autoregressive mechanisms. It establishes that FlowAR's computational capabilities can be bounded by TC0 circuits with constant depth and polynomial width, highlighting new theoretical limitations.

**2. Technical Approach:**  
- **Circuit Complexity Analysis:** Uses threshold circuits (TC0) with O(1) depth and polynomial width to model FlowAR's computational limits.  
- **Low-Rank Approximations:** Employs these to create efficient model variants, aligning with theoretical criteria.  
- **Theoretical Bounds:** Derives metrics for computational efficiency and expressiveness, linking architectural choices to performance.

**3. Quantitative Findings:**  
- **Simulation Feasibility:** FlowAR models with feature maps of size n×n×c are simulable by TC0 circuits.  
- **Time Complexity:** Computations can achieve almost quadratic time under certain conditions.  
- **Model Variants:** Efficient constructions using low-rank approximations validate theoretical predictions.

**4. Limitations & Assumptions:**  
- **Feature Map Constraints:** The analysis assumes specific feature map dimensions, limiting applicability to varying architectures.  
- **Approximation Errors:** Low-rank approximations may introduce inaccuracies affecting model fidelity.  
- **Theoretical Scope:** Focuses on TC0 circuits, excluding other circuit classes, and assumes idealized conditions for analysis.

**5. Domain Impact (Theoretical/Practical):**  
- **Theoretical:** Advances understanding of computational limits in generative models, guiding future architectures.  
- **Practical:** Offers insights for developing more efficient implementations, enhancing model scalability and performance.  

This structured approach provides a foundational analysis for FlowAR models, contributing to both theoretical understanding and practical applications in generative tasks.
